subject.title: feat(llama-cpp): RAM-gated Gemma 4 E4B default, drop Qwen

question: After the constrained-memory bug is fixed, should llama-cpp replace Qwen with Gemma 4 E4B and omit the bundled-download offer entirely below 16 GiB?
rationale: This changes the provider’s default model and deliberately removes an onboarding route from lower-memory machines; benchmarks support the proposal, but repository-visible maintainer approval is required for that product tradeoff.

options.title: Approve gated Gemma
options.body: Adopt Gemma as the sole bundled default after making the RAM check constraint-aware and adding real onboarding/download proof.

options.title: Keep a tiered fallback
options.body: Offer Gemma on eligible systems while retaining a smaller verified model for lower-memory machines.

options.title: Pause the default swap
options.body: Keep the current default until unified onboarding can hide unavailable candidates and explain hardware requirements before selection.

recommendation.title: Approve gated Gemma
recommendation.body: Adopt Gemma as the sole bundled default after making the RAM check constraint-aware and adding real onboarding/download proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the provider/default and the related model-ranking benchmarks, giving them the strongest available context for the policy decision.
